nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $N$ be natural numbers, and let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers with $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ that is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$. Then $|S| \le r_k(N)$, where $r_k(N)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ containing no nontrivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.
nodes.title: Progression-free subsets are bounded by the extremal size

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. If a set $s \subseteq M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$, then $s$ has exactly $l$ elements, counting the size of an infinite set as $\infty$.
nodes.title: Cardinality of a set arithmetic progression

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. If a set $s \subseteq M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$, then there are $a, d \in M$ with $s = \{a + n d : n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < l\}$, where $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.
nodes.title: First term and difference of a set arithmetic progression

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $\beta$ a preordered type, $f : \beta \to M$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ contains a monotone arithmetic progression of length $k$ if there are $x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_k$ in $\beta$ such that the list $(f(x_1), \dots, f(x_k))$ is an arithmetic progression of length $k$: for some $a, d \in M$ it equals $(a, a + d, \dots, a + (k - 1)d)$ or its reverse.
nodes.title: Monotone arithmetic progressions in a function

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N}$. A list $s$ of elements of $M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ if there are $a, d \in M$ such that $s = (a, a + d, \dots, a + (l - 1)d)$ or $s = (a + (l - 1)d, \dots, a + d, a)$, where $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions of lists

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. A finite set $s \subseteq M$ is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $l$ if it is so as a set: $l \le 1$, or no subset of $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$.
nodes.title: Progression-free finite sets

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a set of natural numbers such that $a = b$ whenever $a, b, c \in s$ satisfy $a + c = 2b$. Then $s$ is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $3$: no subset of $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $3$.
nodes.title: Sets of naturals without three-term progressions

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. A set $s \subseteq M$ is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $l$ if every subset of $s$ that is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ forces $l \le 1$; equivalently, $l \le 1$ or no subset of $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$.
nodes.title: Progression-free sets

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $l \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a, d \in M$. A list $s$ of elements of $M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ starting from $a$ with difference $d$, in either direction, if $s = (a, a + d, \dots, a + (l - 1)d)$ or $s = (a + (l - 1)d, \dots, a + d, a)$, where $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$; when $l = 0$ both lists are empty.
nodes.title: List arithmetic progressions with given start and difference

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and $a, d \in M$. A set $s \subseteq M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ with first term $a$ and difference $d$ if $s = \{a + n d : n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < l\}$ and $s$ has exactly $l$ elements, counting the size of an infinite set as $\infty$; here $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.
nodes.title: Set arithmetic progressions with given first term and difference

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. A set $s \subseteq \alpha$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ if there are $a, d \in \alpha$ such that $s = \{a + nd : n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < l\}$ and $s$ has exactly $l$ elements (infinitely many when $l = \infty$). Here $nd$ denotes the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.
nodes.title: Sets that are arithmetic progressions

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $N$, the largest size $r_k(N)$ of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$ satisfies $r_k(N) \le N$.
nodes.title: Trivial upper bound for the largest progression-free subset

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $N$, let $r_k(N)$ be the largest size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$. Then some subset $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$ has exactly $r_k(N)$ elements.
nodes.title: A largest progression-free subset is attained

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $N$, $r_k(N)$ is the largest cardinality of a subset $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ that is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$, meaning that if $k \ge 2$ then no subset of $S$ is an arithmetic progression of length $k$ (for $k \le 1$ every subset qualifies).
nodes.title: Largest size of a progression-free subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a set in an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ with $l > 1$. If $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$, then $s$ is not free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $l$.
nodes.title: A progression of length greater than one is not progression-free

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
